title: BACKGROUNDS - the bg field, on five different slide types: photo, gradient, texture.

slides.name: 01-photo-cover
slides.sub: Every slide type takes a bg. A photo sits behind the content, a scrim keeps the type readable, and the linter measures the contrast instead of trusting it.

slides.name: 02-gradient
slides.headline: TWO TOKENS AND AN ANGLE
slides.micro: from and to name palette tokens, never raw css. a deck cannot write into a style attribute.

slides.name: 03-texture-concrete
slides.headline: SIX TILES. EVERY SLIDE A DIFFERENT CORNER
slides.micro: felt, grain, scan, paper, concrete, halftone. the offset is seeded from the deck slug and the slide number, so two slides never show the same patch, and tomorrow renders the same file.

slides.name: 04-photo-on-paper
slides.headline: ON PAPER THE SCRIM GOES WHITE
slides.micro: dim is the opacity of a flat plane in the slide's own base colour. on ink it darkens, on paper it lightens. getting that backwards is the fastest way to make a slide unreadable.

slides.name: 05-halftone-cta
slides.headline: RUN THE LINTER BEFORE YOU POST
actions: It measures contrast under every line of type.
